found_during: A6b pre-ACCEPT read, before any action
defect: permits_triggers() has no freshness bound. It reports the last recorded state regardless of age, so a 71-hour-old AUTHORIZED observation permits provider triggers while the access token behind it has been dead for roughly 63 hours.
why_it_matters: The same boolean feeds publish.guard(authorized=...). A1c semantics require that an authorization loss render the gate failed, never passed. A stale AUTHORIZED could therefore permit publishing a production SUCCESS while the user authorization is in fact dead — the one direction this programme has refused since A1c.
not_a_false_alarm_because: the store is not merely optimistic: the live probe returns 401, so the recorded state and reality disagree right now, not hypothetically.
class: a stale reading reported as a current fact
action_taken: STOP_PRE_ACCEPT_STATE_CHANGED; nothing was accepted, no provider was contacted, no credential was spent
not_repaired_here: adding a freshness bound changes authorization semantics in production and is the owner's ruling, not an executor's ad hoc fix
